text:
maya: quick sync — I tried the coalescer change on a canary and saw eviction storms for small tenants.
jon: ugh, what was the canary config?
maya: enabled coalesce_window=50ms, tenant_min_credit=0, soft_demote=true
priya: hm tenant_min_credit=0 is dangerous with coalescing. coalescing groups inflight requests and can spike residency.
sam: can you paste the relevant logs?
maya: here — ````
[2025-10-12T14:02:11Z] prefix=tenant:42 in_flight=64 resident=1024 coalesced=8 evict_attempts=12
[2025-10-12T14:02:12Z] prefix=tenant:42 evict_success=10 demote_soft=true
````
jon: looks like coalescer kept piling reads while eviction loop couldn't catch up. soft_demote left a lot of resident entries in limbo.
priya: tradeoff: soft_demote avoids hard handoffs but with coalescing you need a per-tenant admission cap or credit buffer so a noisy tenant doesn't starve eviction.
maya: thought: add tenant_coalesce_limit and make it proportional to active_lease_count. simple formula: tenant_limit = max(4, min(32, active_leases/8))
sam: also add a hysteresis window on eviction scoring so quick re-promote churn doesn't oscillate. maybe decay score over 10s instead of immediate reset.
jon: agree. also we should distinguish coalesced load vs single-request load in metrics (histogram). right now all requests look the same to eviction policy.
priya: +1 on metrics. add gauge: coalesced_inflight_by_tenant and counter: coalesce_batches_started.
maya: what about fairness across tenants on shared slabs? do we implement soft credits that slowly refill?
priya: credits are good. refill_rate tied to tenant_commit (small tenants get base refill). big tenants need to buy credits via QoS or get throttled.
jon: operationally, we should default conservative: tenant_min_credit=2, tenant_coalesce_limit=8, decay_secs=10 for score. make experiment feature flag gated.
sam: canary plan: rollout to 10% nodes, synthetic small-tenant hotkey workload for 1h, watch evict_rate, resident_growth, tail latency.
linda: add alert if resident_growth_rate > 500MB/min per node or evict_retries>20 in 1m.
infra-bot: deploy started: canary:coalesce-adaptive-2025-10-12 — 2 nodes -> 10% -> monitoring hooks attached
maya: test items: 1) race on handoff token when coalesced requests trigger demote+evict concurrently 2) read-after-write correctness if demote happens mid-batch 3) metrics tagging for tenant id.
priya: for (1) I think we need a tiny handshake change: coalescer should snapshot handoff token at batch start and pass it along; if token advances, the batch aborts and retries. cheap and deterministic.
jon: that sounds safe. add unit test that injects token bump during batch and asserts no stale reads.
sam: I'll add integration test that replays production trace for hotkey spikes.
maya: thanks — I'll update the RFC follow-up doc with config defaults and the canary checklist.
priya: TL;DR: coalescing is beneficial but must be tempered by tenant-level caps and credit refill + scoring hysteresis. metrics + alerts first.
jon: sounds like plan. :thumbsup:
